links.outcome: Sensitivity at a single AI threshold (35) by BI-RADS subgroup
links.effect: At threshold 35, sensitivity for BI-RADS 4A was 41.2% (specificity 84.7%) versus 88.7% sensitivity (specificity 70.2%) for 4B/C, showing a single threshold conceals subgroup underperformance.
links.quote: At a threshold of 35, the sensitivity for BI-RADS 4A cases was only 41.2%, with a specificity of 84.7%.

links.outcome: Sensitivity and specificity of category-specific versus single AI cutoffs
links.effect: Youden-optimal thresholds were 19 (4A; sens 0.71, spec 0.64) and 63 (4B/4C; sens 0.82, spec 0.92); a single threshold of 35 cut 4A sensitivity to 41.2%. Thresholds were not selected with clinician input or response capacity.
links.quote: These findings suggest that separate thresholds for different BI-RADS categories are necessary to avoid missing cancers in the BI-RADS 4A group.

links.outcome: AI score discrimination in BI-RADS 4A and discordant cases, supporting decision-support use only
links.effect: AUC 0.685 for 4A; in 4B/4C lesions with AI scores <35, 19.5% were malignant with no significant AI score difference between benign and malignant, so AI cannot be relied on alone.
links.quote: the thresholds should be applied with caution, as current AI systems may not be reliable enough for independent decision-making in the absence of radiologist input.

links.effect: 41 BI-RADS 4B/4C cases had AI scores <35; 8 (19.5%) were malignant, so low AI scores can miss cancers.
links.quote: Eight malignant cases (19.5%) were confirmed, including six DCIS and two IDC.
